Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

PACE 0.99.20

  • The core carries its own trigamma(), so the solver no longer depends on R supplying one. Agrees with R’s to 1.8e-15 across the range it is used over.

PACE 0.99.19

  • Declares its dependency on S4Vectors, which stashPACE() uses.

PACE 0.99.18

  • Condition signals build their messages without paste(), and the ridge check handles empty input directly rather than suppressing the warning it would raise.

PACE 0.99.17

  • New compactFit() drops the per-cell matrices before saving a fit, which the vignette previously did by assigning into a slot.
  • The vignettes read fits through accessors rather than @, which clears BiocCheck’s note about slot access in examples and vignettes.

PACE 0.99.16

  • New stashPACE() copies a fit’s readouts into metadata(spe), so results can travel with the data they came from. The solver state is not copied.

PACE 0.99.15

  • Records the Australian Government Research Training Program as funder in Authors@R.

PACE 0.99.14

  • PACEFit gains a validity method. Replacing a slot wholesale used to pass silently and break every readout downstream; fit@fit <- list() is now refused.
  • New accessors cellTypes(), paceParams() and fitState(), and validated replacement methods for neighbourSlopes(), varianceDecomposition() and topDrivers().

PACE 0.99.13

  • verbose = FALSE is now silent. The shrinkage step reported its progress regardless, because it never received the flag, and mashr printed its own on top of that.
  • Installation instructions use BiocManager::install().
  • The vignette evaluates every chunk.
  • Minimum R version is 4.6.0.

PACE 0.99.12

  • plotDecomposition() draws the zoom panel’s percentage labels upright, so that neighbouring bars of similar height no longer overlap each other’s text.

PACE 0.99.11

  • Added a canonical multivariate adaptive shrinkage implementation to the compiled core, alongside the existing mashr path. It reproduces mashr’s calls exactly on both reference cohorts.

PACE 0.99.10

  • The driver score columns are named for what the method calls them: driver_score and driver_score_spec4, previously MCSD and MCSD4. plotDrivers() takes panels = "score" in place of "mcsd".

PACE 0.99.9

  • topDrivers() documents which model term each column holds. On a fit with a condition the table carries two different slopes, and they are not a raw and shrunken pair of the same quantity.
  • The condition vignette shows the responder decomposition and driver figures, and prints the driver table.

PACE 0.99.6

  • The per-pair gene score is called the driver score throughout the documentation and plot labels, matching the method description.

PACE 0.99.4

  • Fixed portability defects found by the Bioconductor build matrix: bit identity on arm64, a crash on Windows from static thread_local destructors, an unsupported system2(env=) on Windows, and missing -pthread on compile flags for Wasm.

PACE 0.99.0

  • Initial Bioconductor submission.
